sources.scope: 2026–27 English BA History EER clauses 3.2, 3.3, 3.5 and Appendices 1–2. Controls route, English course codes, blocks and credits.
Public BA overview. Corroborates historical content and interests. The 2026 cohort regulations and student curriculum govern where the Year 2 presentation differs.
Seven specialisations in two tracks, and the writing and theory components.
The 30 EC coherent elective package, 30 EC free electives, level rules and external approval.
Official graduate and further-study examples, used for search context.
Supervised 15 EC bachelor thesis in the final year.
Official student curriculum specifically for the 2026 entry. Confirms two core profiles, four-period package, writing and theory, profiling and thesis.
Writing Skills for Historians, period 1. Writing in genres for academic and public audiences and 45 EC introductory threshold.
Theory of History, period 2. Historiography, objectivity and historical practice, and 45 EC introductory threshold.
Research Seminar A, period 3, 45 EC introductory threshold and historical research. The module code is shared with the Dutch cohort example.
English BA individual thesis, 15 EC, two periods. Before entry, complete at least 30 EC at level 3 including Research Seminar A. The outline must be sufficient before proceeding.

curriculum: The September 2026 full-time English BA contains a 120 EC major and 60 EC profiling space. The first listed track and package are History and Foundations of Europe. The major includes 60 EC of core study, 30 EC of specialisation, 7.5 EC Writing Skills for Historians, 7.5 EC Theory of History and a 15 EC individual thesis. The 60 EC profiling space includes a 30 EC coherent minor or approved study abroad and 30 EC free choice, with an internship up to 15 EC. At least 15 EC of profiling is at levels 2–3. The English EER and explicit 2026 cohort student schedule govern over the recruitment page’s Year 2 connecting-module description. The English course list is checked independently from the Dutch case.
progression: The first year pairs chronological study with disciplinary or methods study, with 45 introductory EC across the first-year core. In Year 2 Power, Religion and Identity, Cities and Citizens, Seminar A and Seminar B run in order across the four periods. Writing Skills for Historians and Theory of History run in periods 1 and 2 and require 45 introductory EC, as does Seminar A. Before the two-period thesis students complete 30 EC at level 3 including Seminar A. The 30 EC package, 7.5 EC theory and 15 EC thesis satisfy the 45 EC advanced major requirement. The thesis is individual and starts with a qualifying outline.
components: Introduction to History as a Discipline (GE1V16002)
The 30 EC Foundations of Europe package starts here. Its four courses run in sequence across the four teaching periods.
Research Seminar A: Foundations of Europe (GE3V21001)
The seminar requires 45 EC at introductory level and contributes to thesis entry.
Research Seminar B: Foundations of Europe (GE3V21015)
Writing Skills for Historians and Theory of History each require 45 EC at introductory level.
Students must earn at least 30 EC at advanced level and complete a qualifying Research Seminar A before starting the 15 EC thesis.
Choose a minor or approved study abroad. Across the full 60 EC of electives, at least 15 EC must be at level 2 or 3.
Options include individual courses, a second minor or an internship of up to 15 EC.
